messages:
emily: Heads up — we're getting a customer escalation from AcmeCorp. p95 and p99 for text-generation routes spiked right after runtime v2.3.1 rollout (20% traffic). Graph: https://dash/redwood/runtime/p95?cohort=acme :eyes:

sam: Do we have the canary cohort breakdown? was the canary showing the same trend?

emily: Canary (5% cohort) had a small blip but within noise. The 20% ramp started at 02:12 UTC and spike shows at 02:20. p95 up ~2.3x, p99 up ~4x. No increase in error-rate.

nate: Any binding changes in that runtime? kernel-selector / scheduler tweaks?

emily: v2.3.1 includes the new schedule_bias allocator + kernel selector fallback for T4s. Release notes: "improved batch packing; changed default max_batch_tokens from 2048 -> 4096"

maria: That max_batch_tokens bump stands out — can cause queuing if sequence lengths are mixed. Can you dump sample request size distribution for acme?

emily: Pasted sample from logs (first 2k requests after spike):
```
seq_len_hist: {8: 310, 32: 420, 256: 880, 1024: 390}
avg_seq: 340
median_seq: 256
```
Looks like heavy long-tail in that tenant.

sam: If batch window grew, long sequences would block short ones -> tail latency. Check queueing metrics: runtime/queue_depth, batch_watermark, batch_latency.

emily: queue_depth jumped from 6->28 during spike, batch_latency 25ms -> 240ms, avg_tokens_per_batch up 3x.

nate: Hypothesis: larger max_batch_tokens allowed runtime to pack long sequences into same batch, increasing head-of-line wait for short requests = pathological queuing. Two mitigations: roll max_batch_tokens back OR enable short-request prioritization.

maria: We should bisect config change quickly. Can we reproduce in a sandbox by replaying Acme traffic?

emily: I kicked off a synthetic replay to the staging cluster: `/tools/replay --cohort acme --start 02:10 --rate 1x` Started at 03:05. Early results: staging shows same p95 bump when max_batch_tokens=4096.

sam: Good repro. Next step: test two quick fixes in staging: 1) restore max_batch_tokens=2048 2) enable batch_time_cap=25ms (force flush). Which is lower risk?

nate: Restore max_batch_tokens first (fast config flip), then test batch_time_cap. Also run a bisect to confirm change set: `/deploy/bisect --between v2.3.0 v2.3.1 --tests p95,p99 --cohort acme`

emily: Bisect results: change delta points to config blob `runtime/scheduler: default.max_batch_tokens` as principal delta. test outputs attached (short).

infra-bot: deploy note: rollback flag created for v2.3.1 -> v2.3.0 on canary traffic routing. Use `/deploy rollback --id v2.3.1 --scope cohort:canary` to apply.

maria: Let's prepare customer communication. Support needs ETA for mitigation. If we flip config on all clusters, we need a short maintenance window or can do gradual patch.

emily: I applied config flip on canary at 03:28: `/runtime/config set default.max_batch_tokens=2048 --scope cohort:canary`. Canary p99 dropped back to baseline within 90s.

sam: Great. Emily, can you promote the config change to 20% cohort? Use staged rollout and monitor p95/p99 and queue_depth.

emily: Rolling to 20% now. Command: `/runtime/rollout config:default.max_batch_tokens=2048 --to 20% --watch`

emily: Update: at +4min after rollout, p95 back to normal, p99 trending down, queue_depth stabilized.

maria: Support-bot: please send status update to Acme with note: "We've identified a batching config change in recent runtime version that increased queueing for long-tail sequences; we've reverted that config for your traffic. Monitoring now."

support-bot: Sent message to AcmeCorp customer account. Ticket updated: #AC-4321.

nate: Follow-ups: add targeted test in pre-rollout suite: synthetic cohort with mixed sequence length (heavy tail) to catch regressions. Also add policy to disallow max_batch_tokens > 4096 without perf signoff.

sam: And add a runtime safeguard: if batch_latency > 150ms for 1m and queue_depth > 10, auto-flip batch_time_cap to 25ms for that cohort. Lower risk than full rollback.

emily: I'll file two tickets: PERF-1205 (pre-rollout mixed-length greenbox test) and RUNTIME-1402 (auto-flush safety trigger).

maria: Nice. Once PRs are up, run full replay and confirm no regressions for other tenants.

emily: Logs + replay artifacts uploaded: https://s3.redwood/replays/9176543210-acme-replay.tar.gz

sam: Great work. Closing loop: keep monitoring next 6 hours, if anything reappears escalate to priority-alpha. :thumbsup:

nate: Quick note for release owners — for future kernel/scheduler changes, include an explicit queueing model doc and a canary test that purposely skews sequence length distribution.

emily: Will do. Adding to release checklist. :white_check_mark:
